text: In the cold testing corridor outside Vantry, the maglev prototype reached a recorded top speed of 540 km/h during a midnight run on 17 October, according to engineers at the Avenport Transit Authority. The train, a silver three-car unit known as VM-3, had been built over seven years of incremental trials after the region’s old rail network buckled under freight demand. On the final pass, sensors along the 14-kilometre guideway logged stable levitation and no structural warning flags, despite gusting crosswinds over the salt flats. Project director Mirelle Sorn said the result “moves high-speed travel from promise into schedule,” though she cautioned that passenger service remains at least two winters away.
